Definition: from G3982; objectively, trustworthy; subjectively, trustful:--believe(-ing, -r), faithful(-ly), sure, true.
KeyPassages: 1 Corinthians 1:9; 1 John 1:9; 2 Timothy 2:13; Hebrews 11:11; Matthew 25:21; Revelation 2:10
BiblicalUsage: Pistos means faithful and trustworthy — of God, and of His people. God is faithful, says 1 Corinthians 1:9, and He is faithful and just to forgive us in 1 John 1:9. If we believe not, yet He abides faithful, says 2 Timothy 2:13, and Sarah judged Him faithful who had promised in Hebrews 11:11. Jesus calls the servant good and faithful in Matthew 25:21, and promises the crown of life to the faithful unto death in Revelation 2:10.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe faithfulness runs both ways: God is faithful to me, and I am to be faithful to Him. My position is that His faithfulness is the ground of mine — I can be faithful because He cannot deny Himself.
RelatedBooks: 1 Corinthians; 1 John; 2 Timothy; Hebrews; Matthew; Revelation
